about: SDK 3.0.0 additions to shared recordings (make_sharing.py holds the rules and the reference): the feed's pre-roll ring and tail, the take list with a feed, take_seq and gap_ms_prev, and the take list answers. Per case: `flags` of the signed config, whether sharing is on with the learner's yes at the start, and `events` in order. A feed event (the wall time of the call, its samples and rate) expects where its samples went (`to_tail`, `to_ring`, `dropped`) and the ring's size after it; a take event expects its `pre_roll`, whether it was recorded and joined, and the samples fed during it that were dropped; `held` true when its audio was held under the cap (30 s or less of room), and `cut_at_take_samples` when the recording reached the cap inside it: the index, among the take's own samples from 0, of the first sample of the new recording. `recordings`: every recording in order with its rate, stream samples, audio_ms (floor), take_seq, gap_ms_prev (null: absent; 0: present with 0), the take list (null: one take, none sent) and `parts`, the samples of each take's pre-roll, own audio and tail in stream order (a cut take has a part in both recordings); `deleted` marks a recording whose queue was deleted (sharing off, or "Delete what I shared"), `closed_at_cap` one that closed because its audio reached 20 minutes (a whole recording: `completed` true).

cases.name: pre-roll and tail at 16 kHz
cases.about: The app feeds for 3 s before the take and 1 s after it: the last 1 s of the feed (16000 samples) is prepended, the first 0.5 s after the take (8000) is appended, the rest of the feed stays in the ring. One take: no take list.

cases.name: pre-roll and tail at 48 kHz
cases.about: The same with a 48 kHz microphone: 48000 and 24000 samples.

cases.name: a feed shorter than 1 s
cases.about: 0.4 s of feed before the take: the pre-roll is those 6400 samples. Nothing is fed afterwards: no tail.

cases.name: a feed that stops before the take
cases.about: The feed stopped 2 s before the take started: its audio does not lead into the take and is discarded.

cases.name: a feed that pauses and comes back
cases.about: The feed pauses for 1.5 s and returns 0.3 s before the take: the ring is emptied at the pause, so the pre-roll is the last 0.3 s only, not 0.3 s glued to older audio.

cases.name: a feed that starts late after the take
cases.about: Nothing is fed for 1 s after the take, then the feed returns: it does not continue the take, so there is no tail; it fills the ring.

cases.name: the learner has not said yes
cases.about: Sharing is not on: every fed buffer is dropped at once, the ring stays empty, the take is not recorded.

cases.name: sharing goes off while the ring holds audio
cases.about: The ring holds 1 s when the learner switches sharing off: it is emptied at once, later buffers are dropped, and the take after it is not recorded. Switched on again, the feed counts from there.

cases.name: two takes 2 s apart with a continuous feed
cases.about: One recording. Between the takes 2 s are fed: 0.5 s is the first take's tail, the last 1 s is the second take's pre-roll, the 0.5 s between them is not kept. The take list: the first take starts after its pre-roll (1000 ms), the second at 1000 + 5000 + 500 + 1000 ms; gap_ms is the wall gap, 2000.

cases.name: two takes 1.2 s apart with a continuous feed
cases.about: The 1.2 s between the takes are all kept: 0.5 s as the tail, 0.7 s as the pre-roll.

cases.name: two takes 4 s apart
cases.about: Over the window: two recordings, take_seq 1 and 2, gap_ms_prev 4000 on the second. The second gets its own pre-roll from the feed.

cases.name: take_seq and gap_ms_prev
cases.about: Five recordings of one install: 30 minutes and 49 ms after the first (rounded to 1800000), exactly one hour after the second (3600000), one hour and 1 ms after the third (absent), then after "Delete what I shared" (the server took it, so sharing went off) and sharing turned on again with the switch, the count starts again at 1 with no gap.

cases.name: the feed has another rate than the take
cases.about: A 48 kHz feed and a 16 kHz take: no pre-roll (the ring is discarded) and no tail (the buffer after the take ends the tail and goes to a 48 kHz ring).

cases.name: a buffer fed during a take
cases.about: The app keeps feeding while the take runs: those 32000 samples are dropped.

cases.name: the join window 0 still records a tail
cases.about: share_join_ms 0 never joins takes, and the tail of the first take is still recorded before its recording closes. The second take, 0.3 s later, starts a new recording; the ring is empty because the feed went to the tail.

cases.name: the tail wait: one buffer of 1.4 s that ends 1.4 s after the take still gives the tail
cases.about: The feed call comes 1400 ms after the take's end with 1.4 s of audio: it continues from the take (F3) and is inside the 1500 ms tail wait, so its first 8000 samples are the tail and the rest goes to the ring.

cases.name: the tail wait: a buffer that ends 1.6 s after the take is too late for the tail
cases.about: 1.6 s of audio in one call 1600 ms after the take's end: it continues from the take (F3), but the tail wait of 1500 ms is over, so nothing goes to the tail and the ring takes its last 1 s. The recording is still open (the window is 3 s): the take 100 ms later joins it with that pre-roll.

cases.name: the tail wait with the join window 0: the recording has closed without a tail
cases.about: share_join_ms 0 and no feed for 1500 ms after the take: the recording closes there without a tail. The buffer that ends 1600 ms after the take goes to the ring, and the next take starts a new recording with it as pre-roll.

cases.name: the app goes to the background
cases.about: The background closes the recording and empties the ring: the take after it has no pre-roll and starts a new recording.

cases.name: buffers of one second
cases.about: An app that feeds 1 s buffers: a call arriving 1 s after the previous one continues the feed (its own audio lasts that long), so the ring holds the last buffer and the tail takes half of the first buffer after the take.

cases.name: no feed at all
cases.about: An app that captures only during takes: no pre-roll, no tail; exactly 2.0.3, plus take_seq.

cases.name: odd sample counts with a feed
cases.about: start_ms is floor(1000 * samples before the take / rate) on the real sample counts.

cases.name: the cap inside a take: 31 s of room, a take of 60 s
cases.about: The recording holds 1169 s when a take joins it 1 s later: 31 s of room is more than 30 s, so the take is written as it comes. Its first 496,000 samples (31 s) fill the recording to 19,200,000 samples, which closes at the cap with a take list of two entries; its sample 496,000 opens a new recording: take_seq 2, gap_ms_prev 0, 29 s, one take, no take list.

cases.name: the cap inside a take at 48 kHz
cases.about: The same at 48 kHz: the cut is after 1,488,000 samples of the take, at 57,600,000 samples of the recording.

cases.name: a later take joins the continuation
cases.about: After the cut the continuation is an ordinary recording: a take 1 s after the cut take's end joins it, with start_ms 29000 (the 29 s that continued).

cases.name: 30 s of room: the take is held, fits and joins
cases.about: The recording holds 1170 s: exactly 30 s of room, so the take 1 s later is held. It ends after 20 s, which fits: it joins, and the recording holds 1190 s.

cases.name: 30 s of room: a held take of exactly 30 s fills the recording
cases.about: 1170 s + 30 s is not more than 20 minutes: the take joins, the recording reaches 19,200,000 samples on the take's last sample and closes at the cap. Nothing continues. The take after it starts a new recording with the real gap_ms_prev (1000).

cases.name: 30 s of room: a held take that runs 60 s starts a new recording
cases.about: The held take outgrows the room: the recording closes without it at 1170 s (not at the cap; one take, no take list) and the take starts a new recording with all its 60 s, take_seq 2 and the real gap_ms_prev (1000). Nothing is cut.

cases.name: 30.001 s of room is not held, with odd sample counts
cases.about: The recording holds 18,719,991 samples (1169999 ms, floor): the room is 30001 ms, so the take is not held and is cut after 480,009 samples, where the recording reaches 19,200,000. start_ms of the cut take is 1169999.

cases.name: the fit is in samples: a held take 5 samples too long starts a new recording
cases.about: The recording holds 18,720,015 samples (1170000 ms, floor): 479,985 samples of room, so the take is held. Its 479,990 samples are 29999 ms (floor), and 1170000 + 29999 fits in floored ms, but the samples pass the cap by 5: the take does not fit. The recording closes without it and the take starts a new recording whole.

cases.name: the fit is in samples: the same take 5 samples shorter fills the recording
cases.about: 479,985 samples are exactly the room: the held take joins, the recording reaches 19,200,000 samples and closes at the cap. Nothing continues.

cases.name: the fit is in samples at 48 kHz: 17 samples too long
cases.about: 56,160,047 samples in the recording (1170000 ms, floor), 1,439,953 of room. A held take of 1,439,970 samples (29999 ms, floor) fits in floored ms and passes the cap by 17 samples: it starts a new recording whole.

cases.name: the fit is in samples at 48 kHz: the take that fills the recording exactly
cases.about: 1,439,953 samples: the held take joins and the recording closes at the cap on its last sample.

cases.name: a first take of exactly 20 minutes
cases.about: A take that reaches the Session's limit: the recording closes at the cap on the take's last sample and nothing continues. The audio fed after it has no recording to go to (no tail) and fills the ring; the next take, 2 s later, starts a new recording with that pre-roll, take_seq 2 and gap_ms_prev 2000.

cases.name: a first take of exactly 20 minutes at 48 kHz
cases.about: 57,600,000 samples: one recording, closed at the cap.

cases.name: the pre-roll counts against the cap: a first take of 20 minutes with 1 s of pre-roll
cases.about: The recording starts with 16000 samples of pre-roll, so the take's first 19,184,000 samples (1199 s) fill it. The take's last second continues in a new recording with gap_ms_prev 0 and no pre-roll.

cases.name: the pre-roll counts against the cap at 48 kHz
cases.about: 48000 samples of pre-roll: the cut is after 57,552,000 samples of the take.

cases.name: the pre-roll counts in the hold: 30 s of room, 1 s of pre-roll and a take of 29.5 s
cases.about: The first take's tail brings the recording to 1170 s. The next take is held with its 1 s of pre-roll: 30.5 s do not fit in 30 s, so it starts a new recording with the pre-roll and all its audio (the sole take's start_ms would be 1000) and gap_ms_prev 1500.

cases.name: the same take without a pre-roll fits
cases.about: The feed stops after the tail, so there is no pre-roll: the held take of 29.5 s fits in the 30 s and joins.

cases.name: the longest cut: 31 s of room, 1 s of pre-roll, a take of 20 minutes
cases.about: The recording holds 1169 s with its tail. The take joins with its pre-roll and is cut after 480,000 of its samples (30 s). 1170 s continue in the new recording, which stays under the cap: a take never crosses it twice.

cases.name: the tail is cut at the cap
cases.about: The recording holds 1199.8 s when its take ends. Of the audio fed after it 3200 samples (0.2 s) fill the recording, which closes at the cap; the rest goes to the ring and no recording is opened.

take_list_answers.about: POST /v1/uploads/{id}/takes: the answers in order and the list's state after each (pending: kept and retried on the outbox's backoff; done; dropped). `issue_reported_now` is true on the one answer that reports the bad-request issue. Changed on 2026-11-11: 400 keeps the list pending (2.0.3 dropped it).

cases.name: accepted
refused with 400, then accepted after the server was fixed
refused with 400 until sharing goes off
refused with 400 until the recording is seven days old
a server without the route
the upload was deleted
the token expired
the server is busy, then refuses, then accepts
